claims.nodeLabel: AARO Report on the Historical Record of U.S. Government Involvement with UAP, Volume I
claims.text: AARO confirms in an official report that a proposal to 'reverse-engineer any recovered off-world spacecraft' was formally submitted to DHS as a Prospective Special Access Program by people who had run the DIA program. A PSAP submission is a bureaucratic instrument, not a rumour: it means the recovery premise was carried into formal special-access channels twice (Reid's 2009 SAP request, and KONA BLUE), and was refused both times on merit/classification grounds rather than on the grounds that the subject matter was fictitious.

claims.nodeLabel: AARO Report on the Historical Record of U.S. Government Involvement with UAP, Volume I
claims.text: AARO's report is itself an artifact of the concealment posture it purports to close out: it confirms the appropriation, the program, the contractor activity and the attempted transfer to DHS, while declining to name the contractor, the program manager, or the DIRD authors — the same redaction boundary DIA drew in the FOIA release.

claims.nodeLabel: Advanced Aerospace Threat Identification Program (AATIP / AAITP)
claims.text: AARO Historical Record Report Vol. I states: 'Unlike AAWSAP, AATIP was never an official DoD program. However, after AAWSAP was cancelled, the AATIP moniker was used by some individuals associated with an informal, unofficial UAP community of interest within DoD that researched UAP sightings from military observers as part of their ancillary job duties.'

claims.nodeLabel: Advanced Aerospace Threat Identification Program (AATIP / AAITP)
claims.text: AARO's formulation is the load-bearing denial artifact: it concedes an actual DoD community of interest researching military UAP sightings, then denies it program status on a naming technicality. DIA's own 2009 correspondence uses 'AAITP' and 'AAWSAP' interchangeably for the same contract, so the 'never an official DoD program' line depends entirely on which of the two names is treated as canonical.

b.label: Waived unacknowledged special access program (waived USAP)

edges.label: contractor disclosure to Congress requires SAPCO approval
edges.note: The office is where the designation is administered. DoDD 5205.07 establishes DoD SAPCO 'under the authority, direction, and control of the Deputy Secretary of Defense', and DoDI 5205.11 para. 1.2.f gives the Secretary the power to designate select unacknowledged SAPs as waived. The waiver is a statutory power exercised through this structure.

edges.label: Reid is the principal behind the 2008-2009 DIA engagements
edges.note: AARO's official history states: 'At the direction of Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid (D-NV), the Defense Appropriations Acts of Fiscal Years 2008 and 2010 appropriated $22 million for the DIA to assess long-term and over-the-horizon foreign advanced aerospace threats to the United States.' It further records that on 24 June 2009 Reid wrote to Deputy Secretary of Defense William Lynn III asking that the programme be made a Special Access Program. Tier 2: AARO is an interested party in its own institutional history.

edges.label: Elements and tradecraft

edges.label: Reid's Nevada base; earmark performed by a Las Vegas constituent
edges.note: This is not merely a home-town link. AARO's official history names 'Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid (D-NV)' as having directed the appropriation, and the federal award record places Bigelow's company in Nevada; the money Reid secured was performed by a company in the state he represented. Tier 2 because the constituent relationship is the inference joining those two documented facts, not something either document states.
